title: BulkDestructiveFlow
wrapsNative: sheet(isPresented:) with interactiveDismissDisabled while running, holding a VStack that moves through three phases: MonarchConsequenceList and MonarchTypeToConfirmInput to confirm, ProgressView with .monarchLinear while deleting, MonarchBanner for the result
summary: A recipe, not a component: "Delete 37 leads" confirms a bulk deletion with a sample and its consequences, asks for the count to be typed, runs it with a progress bar while the sheet is locked, then reports the items that failed.
whenToUse: When people delete many selected items at once (from a MonarchBulkActionBar), the deletion cannot be undone, and some items may fail on the server.
whenNotToUse: For one item, or a few with no partial failure, use confirmationDialog. For a change that can be undone, delete at once and offer Undo (see undo-toast). For deleting a whole workspace, use MonarchTypeToConfirmInput with its name in a sheet.

states.name: confirm
states.description: The title with the count, a sample of three names and "+34 more", the consequences, a field asking for the count, and a danger button disabled until the count matches.

states.name: running
states.description: A linear progress bar with "12 of 37 deleted"; the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: done
states.description: A success banner when every item was deleted.

states.name: partial
states.description: A warning banner with "36 of 37 leads deleted" and the items that failed with their reason; the app can offer a retry for those items.

appearance: A sheet on the system's sheet background with Monarch components: the danger MonarchButton, the consequence list's icons and tones, the linear progress style in the accent role, and success or warning banners.
platformNotes: The web BulkDestructiveFlow is a component built on WizardDialog with plural rules (Intl.PluralRules), a typeCountAbove threshold, an optional step-up authentication and a retry step. On iOS it composes existing parts in a sheet, so the app decides the threshold for typing the count, writes plural forms with its String Catalog, and runs re-authentication (for example LocalAuthentication) before the deletion. The web's progress callback is the app's own loop updating a counter. Android plans the same recipe.
accessibility: The title has the header trait; the consequence list reads each consequence with its kind.
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput announces when the typed count matches, and the delete button stays disabled until it does.
The standard ProgressView reads its title and value, so VoiceOver can follow "12 of 37 deleted".
Announce the result with AccessibilityNotification.Announcement when the run ends, since focus does not move.
edgeCases: Lock the sheet with interactiveDismissDisabled while the deletion runs, so it cannot be dismissed half way.
Keep the failed items selected after Done so the person can retry or inspect them.
If nothing could be deleted (the request failed), show the error on the confirmation phase and keep the typed count.
